properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on main c4e1cbd): --read-only was wired into the SERVICE a server builds (into_read_only) and into the one-shot table, and a CLIENT builds neither — it opens no store, has no write guard, and forwards every line to a server somebody else started writable. So the flag was accepted by --remote, --shared, a pointer-attached client and the latent surface, and changed nothing
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-03, item 1b of the VS Code --call fix program, on fact:read-only-is-silently-ignored-by-the-remote-and-shared-clients-2026-10-02.

① OBSERVED on main c4e1cbd (debug binary, scratch stores, isolated HOME; script and logs /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/read-only-clients/measure_clients.py, measure-main*.log): with --read-only, add_requirement through `--remote http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (a plain --http server), through `--shared`, and through a client started in a folder whose .reflow2.toml names a registry-served design (the machine-wide entry's flags) each returned a write receipt, and get_node found the requirement in the server's store after every server stopped. The latent surface (`--only-if-present --read-only`, no design) answered reflow2_start_design by creating .reflow2/ and promoting to a WRITABLE surface; a write then landed. `--shared --read-only` in an opted-in folder (.reflow2/ empty) spawned a daemon that created the store. CONTROL, not affected: plain stdio `--read-only` refused the write ("this reflow2 server is READ-ONLY").

② PRECEDENT: search_design found the finding itself (its WHERE-IT-IS-LOST paragraph read from code, explicitly not walked), fact:call-ignores-read-only-and-the-write-lands-2026-10-02 (the one-shot instance, fixed by item 1) and fact:the-remote-client-sends-no-writes-for-... (the remote client forwards every call unchanged). No recorded cause for the client half.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) each client branch returns in main() before --read-only is read (the position class item 1 fixed); (b) the flag is read but only ever applied through ReflowService::into_read_only, which a client never constructs; (c) the --shared daemon is spawned without --read-only, so the server is writable; (d) the server ignores a client's mode (no channel carries it); (e) I measured the wrong thing (a receipt that is not a write).

④/⑤ MEASURED: (e) refuted — get_node read the node back from the store after the servers stopped. (a) refuted as the cause: `--remote` returns before the flag is read, but `--shared` and the pointer path read cli after it is parsed and still forwarded — position is not what decides. (c) is TRUE but not the cause: an already-running daemon started without --read-only was attached to as well, and a --remote server is not ours to start at all; passing the flag to the daemon would also make every OTHER session on it read-only (first start wins, shared.rs). (d) is the design, not a defect: a server serves many sessions and cannot hold one client's mode. (b) is the cause: grep shows --read-only reaches only into_read_only (service construction: stdio, --http, --serve-shared, registry, ephemeral), LatentService never took it, and the forwarding loops in proxy.rs (run, run_waiting, run_remote_with_notice) took no such argument.

⑥ CLASS: a mode that forwards rather than opens has nowhere for a server-side flag to act, so every forwarding mode silently ignored it, and any new one would. The fix puts the screen in the process the agent talks to and makes the flag a REQUIRED argument of every forwarding entry point, so a new client mode cannot forward without deciding.

⑦ PINNED by tests/every_client_mode_honours_read_only.rs, all 8 observed failing on main first. ⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: a remote server other than reflow2 (a gateway) was exercised only through a stand-in.
